subject.title: fix(hooks): wire message:sending internal hook to user-defined hooks

question: Should user-defined internal `message:sending` hooks remain observation-only and run after plugin rewrite/cancel, or should they become a blocking content-guard API?
rationale: The existing internal hook returns no modification or cancellation result, while the issue and PR describe filtering and guardrail uses; ordering and enforcement semantics therefore require an explicit owner decision rather than an accidental API contract.

options.title: Post-policy observer
options.body: Keep internal hooks fire-and-forget, emit only after plugin rewrite/cancel succeeds, document them as observation and audit events, and use the final content.

options.title: Blocking guardrail API
options.body: Design a separate awaited internal-hook result contract with explicit rewrite, cancellation, timeout, and failure semantics before wiring it into delivery.

options.title: Pre-policy notification
options.body: Retain the current pre-policy fire-and-forget event and explicitly accept that it can report content or sends that never reach the channel.

recommendation.title: Post-policy observer
recommendation.body: Keep internal hooks fire-and-forget, emit only after plugin rewrite/cancel succeeds, document them as observation and audit events, and use the final content.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related exact-once hook work covers the same delivery ordering and security contract across channel paths.
